items.pt:

items.title: Remote applications: what changes when nobody meets you first
items.pt:
A remote job application is not just an office application with a different location. Before anyone schedules a call, your writing, timing, and proof of work may have to do more of the introducing. That does not mean performing a polished online personality. It means making it easy for a busy person to understand how you work when the first contact is written.

items.title: Security testing for QA engineers: what Verizon, IBM and OWASP 2025 tell us
items.pt:
Security work is moving closer to testing. Breaches are costly, attackers often get in through known weaknesses, and US employers keep hiring in the field. Here are three public sources (Verizon, IBM and the US Bureau of Labor Statistics), plus the OWASP Top 10, and what a tester can take from them.

One rule before anything else: security testing is done only on systems you are authorised to test, with the owner's written permission. Everything below rests on that rule.

items.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
items.pt: Multilingual pipelines such as FineWeb2 apply one recipe across a thousand languages, leaving the failure modes of individual languages unanticipated. We use an LLM once, as a corpus debugger rather than a classifier: a tool-using agent explores the corpus through a read-only, budgeted API and compiles each finding into an executable test, which a native speaker then validates.
